transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Singh (Redwood SE); Marta Ruiz (LumenPay Head of Platform); Samir Patel (LumenPay SRE); Olivia Chen (LumenPay PM)

Summary: Quick kickoff to align POC milestones, success criteria, and access gating. Main asks: secure service account/VPC access, define benchmark workloads (latency/throughput/cost), mid-point review cadence, exec readout format. Security and data residency/questions flagged as blockers for exec sign-off.

Topics: kickoff timeline; access checklist; workload sizing; p95 latency and throughput targets; bench infra (H100 vs A100 vs GPU pool); security (SOC2, KMS, SSO); milestone dates and exec readout plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Priya, our systems engineering lead. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Marta Ruiz: Hi Jordan, doing well. Thanks. We have about 50 minutes, we wanted to get the POC milestones set and understand what you need for access.
[00:20] Priya Singh: Great, thanks Marta. Quick agenda: kickoff, access gating, benchmark workload sizing, mid-point review dates, and exec readout expectations. We'll also surface common security asks up front so nothing surprises the execs.
[00:35] Samir Patel: Sounds good. Quick context: LumenPay handles high-volume payment memos, low latency is important. We want to try Redwood for payment-descriptions generation and fraud-rerank. Current infra: k8s on GCP, H100 on prem for heavy batches, but prod is split regions.
[00:50] Olivia Chen: We're also sensitive to PII and payment metadata; data residency and audit logs matter for compliance.
[00:58] Jordan Lee: Totally understood. For the POC success criteria, does this list roughly capture it? p95 latency under 800ms for 512-token prompts; able to sustain 10 QPS burst with < 1s tail; cost target below $0.12 per 1k tokens for our workload; functional quality metric — >= 92% on your prompt eval set. Feel free to push back.
[01:20] Marta Ruiz: The latency number seems okay as a starting point — 800ms p95 is acceptable. The cost target I need to discuss with finance but having an estimate is helpful. Quality at 92% sounds strict but fair.
[01:35] Priya Singh: We'll run an initial baseline against an open LLM in our catalog and a Redwood-verified quantized variant. For throughput, we'll test steady-state and burst. We'll also record token-level cost and latency breakdowns so you can see where wins come from (batching, KV cache).
[01:55] Samir Patel: Two questions: 1) How do you want us to provide sample traffic? Is a replay of production logs okay, or do you want synthetic load? 2) Network — we prefer VPC peering over public endpoints for this pilot.
[02:10] Priya Singh: Good Qs. Either works; replay is best for representative lat distributions. For access we support three patterns: hosted keys with IP allowlist, VPC peering for Redwood Private, or an on-prem agent. For a short POC, VPC peering or private endpoints are recommended. We'll send a checklist.
[02:30] Jordan Lee: We'll share a POC access checklist after this call — service-account roles, minimal IAM, VPN/VPC details, and test dataset upload instructions.
[02:40] Olivia Chen: On the security front, our security team will want SOC2 Type II evidence, SSO/SAML integration details, and KMS/HSM options. Also, retention policy — we can't allow model training on customer data.
[02:55] Jordan Lee: Understood. Redwood has SOC2 and can provide ISO artifacts; we also support customer-managed keys via KMS and explicit no-training flags for Private deployments. We'll attach the security pack.
[03:12] Marta Ruiz: Great. Can you outline the proposed milestone dates?
[03:18] Priya Singh: Sure. Proposed milestones: Kickoff (today), Access setup and baseline tests — week 1 (by 2026-11-21), Mid-point review with preliminary benchmarks — day 10 (2026-11-28), Iteration and optimization week — days 11–21, Exec readout and decision window — first week of December (target 2026-12-04). Does that align with your timeline?
[03:42] Samir Patel: That timeline looks aggressive but doable. We need to lock down our SREs for access early — I'll own the service account creation.
[03:55] Olivia Chen: Exec readout needs to include a one-page summary for our CFO and an operations appendix for the SRE team.
[04:05] Jordan Lee: We can provide a concise exec deck template with cost/opportunity slides and an appendix with per-route latency and error breakdowns.
[04:15] Marta Ruiz: For benchmarks, we want three buckets: 1) generation latency under varying prompt lengths (64/256/512 tokens), 2) reranking throughput for 10–50 concurrent jobs, and 3) cost per 1k tokens and cost per decision for rerankers.
[04:35] Priya Singh: We'll prepare a benchmark matrix that includes those buckets. We'll run tests on a few model variants: a smaller quantized model for cost comparisons, and a larger non-quantized for quality checks. We'll note GPU type used — H100 vs A100 — since perf varies.
[04:55] Samir Patel: Can you also measure cold-start for KV cache misses? Our workload has many new sessions so prefix caching behavior matters.
[05:05] Priya Singh: Yes — we'll include cold vs warm KV/cache profiles. We'll also instrument token-level traces so you can see where time is spent.
[05:18] Jordan Lee: Quick note on fallbacks: we can configure a policy to route to a cheaper model when Dedicated capacity spikes or to a hosted variant in a different region to meet SLA. Might be relevant for cost/availability trade-offs.
[05:34] Marta Ruiz: That fallback sounds useful. We need to understand how that affects quality — if fallback lowers quality below the 92% threshold, it's a no-go for some flows.
[05:45] Priya Singh: We'll include a quality delta table showing expected drop for each fallback. We'll also show sample prompts where quality degrades.
[05:58] Olivia Chen: A couple of compliance questions: 1) Data residency — can you ensure tokens processed in EU remain in EU? 2) Audit logs — retainable for 1 year at minimum.
[06:12] Jordan Lee: Yes for EU region pinning on Redwood Private or Hosted with region selection. Audit log retention is configurable and we can push logs to your SIEM via secure forwarder. We'll detail that in the security pack.
[06:28] Samir Patel: About credentials — we'd prefer short-lived tokens and service accounts with least privilege. Also, will the benchmarks incur charges to our cloud bill if you use VPC peering?
[06:40] Priya Singh: Benchmarks run in Redwood's environment won't charge your cloud. If you want the run in your VPC/on-prem, compute costs would be yours. We'll be explicit in the cost estimates.
[06:54] Jordan Lee: Let me read back the milestone plan live so we have alignment: 1) Access & baseline enablement by 2026-11-21; 2) Baseline measurements and initial tuning by 2026-11-24; 3) Mid-point review with preliminary results on 2026-11-28; 4) Optimization sprint and final benching by 2026-12-02; 5) Exec readout week of 2026-12-04.
[07:17] Marta Ruiz: That is acceptable. We might push the exec readout to 12/08 if scheduling conflicts occur but this is a good target.
[07:26] Olivia Chen: Can we confirm who will present at the mid-point review? I'd like both Priya and Samir there; someone from product too.
[07:34] Jordan Lee: We'll have Priya present technical findings, Jordan will present business implications; Marta or Olivia can present LumenPay business context.
[07:45] Samir Patel: One technical ask: can Redwood provide a small harness or script to replay our traffic while anonymizing PII?
[07:55] Priya Singh: Yes — we have a replay harness that supports anonymization rules. We'll provide a template config.
[08:05] Marta Ruiz: Good. On benchmarks, we also want an SLA-style table: target p95, error budget, cost per 1M tokens, and an ops runbook if the latency SLO breaches.
[08:18] Priya Singh: We'll build that into the deliverables: bench matrix + SLO table + short ops runbook for common incidents (fallback triggers, model degradation, rate limiting).
[08:30] Jordan Lee: Quick note about telemetry: Redwood Console will give you token-level cost graphs and per-route dashboards. For the POC we'll grant access to a read-only dashboard for your team.
[08:43] Olivia Chen: Read-only is fine. For the exec readout we want a CSV export of the key metrics so finance can run scenarios.
[08:54] Priya Singh: CSV export is available from the console; we'll include an example export in the mid-point pack.
[09:05] Marta Ruiz: Security again — we need the explicit statement 'no training on customer data' in writing for the exec. Can you add that to the security pack?
[09:15] Jordan Lee: Absolutely — we'll include the no-training clause and the KMS/HSM options.
[09:24] Samir Patel: On the technical deep dive side, if we see model latency variance, can you run profile kernels or share perf counters? We may need kernel-level analysis for our infra team.
[09:35] Priya Singh: We can share anonymized perf counters and stack traces related to serving, subject to NDA on deeper infra details. For on-prem we can also run profiling with your SRE.
[09:48] Olivia Chen: One more thing — do you have experience with reranking pipelines? We use a small ensemble for fraud scoring then rerank and would like best practices for batching vs single-shot rerank.
[09:59] Priya Singh: Yes, we have an ops note: for rerank, batching multiple candidates amortizes token cost and tends to improve throughput, but it can add latency per decision. We'll provide recommendations and a small experiment plan to find the operational sweet spot.
[10:14] Jordan Lee: We're at about 10 minutes left; let's capture the concrete next steps.
[10:20] Marta Ruiz: I'll have Samir create the service account and provide VPC peering details by 2026-11-21.
[10:26] Samir Patel: Yep I'll do that — I'll send details and a contact for our network team.
[10:32] Jordan Lee: Jordan will send access checklist + security pack by 2026-11-20.
[10:36] Priya Singh: Priya will run baseline tests and deliver initial benchmark matrix by 2026-11-24.
[10:42] Olivia Chen: I'll confirm exec attendees and preferred times by 2026-11-25.
[10:48] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Any final questions or blockers?
[10:52] Marta Ruiz: None from me. This is a coherent plan.
[10:56] Samir Patel: No blockers. Looking forward to the harness.
[10:59] Jordan Lee: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the zips: checklist, security pack, and benchmark plan. Midpoint review calendar invite will go out for 2026-11-28.
[11:09] Olivia Chen: Thanks all.
[11:12] Jordan Lee: Thanks, bye.

Recap (auto):
- Access checklist and security pack due 2026-11-20 (Jordan).
- Service account + VPC details due 2026-11-21 (Samir).
- Baseline and benchmark matrix due 2026-11-24 (Priya).
- Midpoint review meeting 2026-11-28.
- Exec readout week of 2026-12-04 (target), confirm by 2026-11-25.

Documents/shared artifacts mentioned: POC access checklist (link to be sent), security pack (SOC2/ISO), baseline benchmark matrix (to be created), replay harness config template (to be provided).

End of transcript.
